## What this was lab about

This lab was about analyzing data from my lab website and  questionaire. I looked at how users interacted with different pages and how classmates responded to questions. I also created graphs to better understand the data. At a high level, I created the graphs and collected the data from the website an survey easily.

## Methods

We used Python with pandas and matplotlib to look at the data. For the website, we checked active users, views per page, and how long people spent on each page. For the survey, we counted how many people answered Yes or No to each question. We used bar graphs to show the patterns.

## Findings

From the survey, most classmates said “Yes” to playing or watching sports, with 12 “Yes” responses compared to 2 “No” responses. This shows that the majority of the class is interested in sports. Figure 2 shows the distribution of these responses.

From the website data, the questionnaire page had the highest average engagement time at 16 seconds per active user and 2.0 views per user. The homepage had 5 views and more total events, but a lower average engagement time of 2.8 seconds. The data page had the least activity, with only 1 view, 1 active user, and 0 seconds of engagement. Figure 1 shows the number of views for each page.

## Discussion

Collecting data like this helps us see which parts of a website people like and how they behave. It also shows us if surveys are working correctly, allowing me to answer any question that is asked.


## Future directions

Future work could include improving the questionnaire to get more responses and better data. We could also track how many people complete the questionnaire and compare that to how many visit the page. Another idea is to look at which pages users spend the most time on and see if that changes over time.
